title: Settlement Agreements: Offer Validity Periods and Recorded-Call Acceptance by Programme
content:
# Settlement Agreements — Offer Validity and Acceptance Channels

Two programme figures of Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements govern how long a written settlement offer stays open and how the consumer may accept it: the offer validity period, in calendar days after the offer date during which the consumer may accept, and whether the programme allows acceptance on a recorded call rather than by electronic signature or in the online portal.

| Figure | Prompt-Pay Discount Settlement | Lump-Sum Settlement | Two-Payment Settlement | Three-Payment Settlement | Six-Payment Settlement | Hardship Settlement |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Offer validity period (calendar days after the offer date) | 10 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 45 |
| Acceptance on a recorded call allowed | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | no |

## Points of judgement

- **Which programmes may be accepted on a recorded call?** The Prompt-Pay Discount, Lump-Sum, Two-Payment and Three-Payment Settlements. The Six-Payment Settlement and the Hardship Settlement are accepted by electronic signature or in the online portal.
- **Which programme stays open longest?** The Hardship Settlement, at 45 calendar days; the Prompt-Pay Discount Settlement is the shortest, at 10.

## Hypothetical illustration

A hypothetical Two-Payment Settlement offer and a hypothetical Hardship Settlement offer made on the same day stay open for 30 and 45 calendar days after that offer date respectively; the consumer may accept the first on a recorded call, but not the second.
